functionality.rationale: The Linux identity provider cannot compile or load its selected Secret Service client if the manifest target or transitive GLib graph is wrong.

security.rationale: libsecret sits on the private identity storage boundary; floating provenance, system fallback, dynamic drift, or accidental non-Linux use is unacceptable.

performance.rationale: libsecret and its GLib transitive graph materially affect Linux clean-build time, cache size, and packaged binary size.

compatibility.rationale: The Linux-only manifest expression and target must work in native, sanitizer, fuzz, and Flutter CMake entrypoints without changing macOS or Windows graphs.

concurrency.rationale: Dependency resolution and link probes introduce no runtime threads, callbacks, shared mutable state, or synchronization contracts.

platform.rationale: libsecret is valid only on Linux while all three desktop platforms share the manifest and CI cache inputs.

persistence.rationale: This task pins and probes a client library but does not create, read, migrate, or delete product records.

adr.rationale: ADR 0006 already selects libsecret; this task records the exact landed dependency and keeps runtime qualification with XT-022.

architecture.rationale: The canonical identity module and private platform-provider boundary are unchanged; this task only supplies the selected dependency.

roadmap.rationale: The P1 execution graph must make libsecret bootstrap an explicit prerequisite of protected identity storage.
